meaning.evidence: "four of the twenty-one quadrilles" and "He may take up the call of the footlights" retain the numbers and uncertainty alongside all the event details.

sense.evidence: "lob in New York" means arrive and "chipped in several old-time tunes" preserves contributing music.

authenticity.evidence: "Tuesday night do" and "along with the missus" are credible colloquial choices, though "brand-spankin'-new" feels rather showy in otherwise restrained prose.

register.evidence: "first big go" offers a light adaptation; most narration such as "The reports added that the hope" remains far short of a level-5 pub yarn.

tone.evidence: "Mr. Ford exclaimed" and the preserved enthusiastic reply retain the report's upbeat curiosity.

flow.evidence: "He was meant to be at the Tuesday night do. But the plans changed" breaks the crowded original into easy spoken units.

variety.evidence: "catch on", "chipped in" and "lob in" vary the idioms without a repeated verbal crutch.

essence.evidence: "help Henry Ford make square dances popular again" preserves the connecting purpose of the Detroit and New York events.

problems.quote: The reports added that the hope in putting on the dance was to help Henry Ford make square dances popular again.
problems.original: It was added that in putting on this dance it was hoped to further Henry Ford's purpose in making square dances again popular.
problems.why: This neutral report style is representative of an adaptation much lighter than the requested full pub-yarn voice.

A.summary: Complete, very readable and accurate, but substantially too restrained for level 5.

meaning.evidence: "he might just answer the call of the footlights" retains the possible contract, and "Word last night" keeps the management report attributed.

sense.evidence: "first big crack at it" and "rock up at the Tuesday night do" convey attempt and attendance correctly.

authenticity.evidence: "more people get keen on 'em" sounds idiomatic, though the pervasive phonetic endings in "bein' got ready for publishin'" look performed.

register.evidence: "Now," and "And the hope, so they reckon" frame a sustained oral retelling suited to level 5; the permitted vulgarity need not be used.

tone.evidence: "Mr. Ford sang out" keeps his spirited enthusiasm and the gently entertaining news character.

flow.evidence: "He was meant to rock up at the Tuesday night do as well. But the plans got changed" gives the change of plan a clear, easy rhythm.

variety.evidence: "big crack", "rock up" and "front up" provide variety, although dropped-g spellings recur conspicuously.

essence.evidence: "help Henry Ford along in makin' square dances popular again" retains the historical report's purpose and colourful fiddler subplot.

problems.why: A sustained layer of phonetic spellings makes the voice feel performed and adds visual friction, despite otherwise plausible idioms.

B.summary: The strongest full-yarn version: faithful and spirited, with some overworked eye dialect.

meaning.evidence: "They reckon puttin' on this dance should help Henry Ford along with gettin' square dances goin' again" softens a specific hope of renewed popularity into restarting the dances.

sense.evidence: "Mr. Ford fair shot back" introduces a slightly defensive sense to the simple exclamation; most other idioms fit.

authenticity.evidence: "more punters'll get keen on 'em" is plausible, but "of them pieces that's bein' got ready to print" feels like a deliberately constructed rustic voice.

register.evidence: "his first big crack at it'll be Tuesday night" and "Dunham'll lob" sustain the strong yarn register without exceeding vulgarity 2.

tone.evidence: "fair shot back" adds a little combativeness to the report, but the lively dance-revival character remains.

flow.evidence: "who's been stayin' as Mr. Ford's guest for a week" begins a very long embedded sentence that buries the planned appearance.

variety.evidence: "big crack", "rock up", "lob" and "punters" vary the vocabulary, though the phonetic ticks dominate the surface.

essence.evidence: "sign up for a vaudeville contract" retains the distinctive detour from Ford's dance event into the fiddler's possible stage career.

problems.why: The reply sounds defensive rather than simply enthusiastic.

problems.quote: of them pieces that's bein' got ready to print
problems.original: of such pieces now being prepared for publication
problems.why: The conspicuously rustic grammar and eye dialect feel staged rather than naturally Australian.
Renewed activity is less specific than renewed popularity.

problems.quote: "Mellie" Dunham, the champion fiddler of Maine, who's been stayin' as Mr. Ford's guest for a week,
problems.original: "Mellie" Dunham, the champion fiddler of Maine, who has been the guest of Mr. Ford for a week,
problems.why: Keeping the extended embedded construction makes the colloquial sentence cumbersome aloud.

C.summary: Strong enough in register and broadly faithful, but strained grammar and a crowded sentence weaken the delivery.
